Chapter 238: 0235 How to Lay Out the Business Strategy

Quite a few singers had been screwed over by Fenbei Wang. In just a few days, Chen Guilong received over twenty emails.

Among these singers, Chen Guilong only recognized Xu Song and Xu Yuteng.

Xu Song had uploaded two songs to Fenbei Wang, *Yanxiao* and *Sanchang Dianying*, and the copyrights had bewilderingly fallen into Fenbei Wang's hands.

Xu Yuteng's case was even more outrageous.

He was a music producer for EMI, but had been idle for a long time. Out of boredom, he had produced over a hundred episodes of a funny Flash short film series.

This year, he wrote a song called *Wait One Minute*, which was originally intended for Huang Pinyuan. But Huang Pinyuan didn't like it, and passing it to Ren Xianqi didn't work out either.

Feeling unwilling to give up, he posted a demo of the song on Fenbei Wang. As a result, Fenbei Wang altered it, gave it to a girl to sing, and even changed the song's title.

Chen Guilong sat in front of his computer, reading the emails from these singers, and began to consider if he could use this opportunity to make something happen.

With the increase in employees and the growth of users on its websites, ByteDance's expenses for the next month were estimated to exceed 4 million yuan. This was mainly for salaries, bandwidth, and server fees.

However, all sources of revenue only amounted to about 2 million yuan per month.

Mobile Weibo was currently profitable, with over 12,000 paying users. But after deducting China Mobile and China Unicom's various revenue shares, as well as the operating fees for Mobile Monternet and Unicom Online, it only earned a few tens of thousands of yuan each month.

Damn it, in this day and age, besides making games, it seemed only Color Ring Back Tones monetized quickly.

Could Xiaonei and Hainei be linked with a music website? The two major websites had so many users; this resource couldn't be wasted. It had to be converted into revenue, just like QQ did with its user base.

He could leverage this lawsuit against Fenbei Wang to launch this initiative.

This matter was different from investing in ZBJ.com.

Investing in ZBJ.com was purely for making money, and it would be easy to cash out in the future.

As for a music website, Chen Guilong planned to acquire one directly and incorporate it into ByteDance's business empire.

Chen Guilong had his employees gather information on music websites and players, and he soon set his sights on TTPlayer.

After initial contact, Chen Guilong found that he couldn't afford it.

Baidu had also targeted TTPlayer and was already in the negotiation stage, with an acquisition price of over 10 million US dollars!

Next, Chen Guilong took a liking to a niche music forum: emumo.

The predecessor of Xiami Music.

It only had about 100,000 users, but it was already profitable and had even rejected an investment from IDG. The founder felt that once capital got involved, the forum would lose its purity.

Hangcheng, Xihu District.

In the same residential complex where Ma Yun started his business, Wang Hao was managing his website.

Wang Hao was a former Alibaba employee who had developed the emumo forum on his own after work. The bizarre name was actually an English acronym for "earn music money."

He had been running the music forum while working at Alibaba, and only recently steeled himself to resign.

Now, Wang Hao was still a one-man army, without a single employee.

But he enjoyed it.

A venture capital firm came knocking? Scram, I don't want your stinking money!

But working for passion alone is difficult.

His phone rang, and Wang Hao, assuming it was a business call, answered, "Hello."

"Hello, Nanguawangmin. I'd like to discuss a collaboration," Chen Guilong said.

Wang Hao asked, "You want a custom exclusive song list?"

"Not a bad idea. But with so many people flooding in at once, my forum's server would crash," Wang Hao asked, "Who is this?"

Chen Guilong said, "Chen Guilong."

Wang Hao suddenly fell silent.

Didn't he want to grow his forum? That was impossible.

He later grew Xiami Music's user base to 12 million.

Unfortunately, it became an abandoned child after being acquired by Alibaba and was essentially run into the ground by the Alibaba team.

Right now, emumo only had 100,000 users, but the vast majority were loyal fans. If he collaborated with Xiaonei and Hainei, the user count could potentially grow to hundreds of thousands or even millions in a short time!

"CEO Chen wouldn't be sending me this colossal amount of traffic for free, would he?" Wang Hao asked.

Chen Guilong said, "I want to acquire emumo. And turn emumo from a music forum into a commercial music platform. You can retain 20% of the shares and continue to be in charge of this platform. I won't interfere with daily operations. For long-term development, I'll only offer suggestions, which you can choose to ignore."

"You'd really give me full authority?" Wang Hao was a little tempted.

Two years ago, he would have rejected it outright.

Just as he had rejected IDG's investment.

But his thinking had changed now; a niche music forum was difficult to sustain. Even if Chen Guilong hadn't appeared, he would have proactively transitioned it into a music platform and launched Xiami Music next year.

Chen Guilong painted a grand picture, "I won't interfere for ten years; we can sign an agreement. Ten years from now, I hope you can become the Vice President of ByteDance in charge of the music division."

"You think that highly of me?" Wang Hao couldn't help but laugh.

Chen Guilong said, "I've looked up your public information. You were a technical director at Alibaba. Being able to resign to start a music forum is enough to prove your boldness and ability."

"I'll fly to Beijing to talk in person," Wang Hao said.

Chen Guilong hung up the phone and sat staring blankly at his computer.

He was thinking.

If ByteDance wanted to grow bigger, relying on just two websites would be very difficult.

It had to expand its business empire. A music platform was one thing, and a video website was another.

Weibo would only truly take off after 2010.

Next would be the short video platform.

With so many projects, he would probably have to venture into the entertainment industry in the future. To run a video website, he'd definitely have to invest in film and television productions himself; otherwise, the copyright fees would be too expensive to afford.

And then there were sites A and B.

Bilibili wouldn't be born for several more years, but AcFun would be online next year.

If Chen Guilong acquired AcFun, or created a similar website himself, it was uncertain whether Bilibili would ever be born.

Because the founder of Bilibili was originally an administrator at AcFun.

Sigh, the management team at AcFun was quite a mess. They spawned Bilibili, they spawned Douyu, yet they themselves ended up barely scraping by.

Guessing the time, he went downstairs to eat.

With more and more companies moving into the Keji Building, even the first-floor cafeteria now had queues.

When would ByteDance get its own cafeteria?

It wasn't necessary yet; there were only about 150 employees in total.

"CEO Chen!"

"Boss."

While getting food in the cafeteria, people would greet Chen Guilong from time to time. Some were his own employees, while others were from other companies in the building.

Chen Guilong was an absolute celebrity here.

Carrying his tray, he found a place to sit and sent a text to Tao Xue: "School's out, right?"

"You know, third-year high school students only get half an hour for each meal. I'm in line for food right now," Tao Xue complained.

Chen Guilong typed, "The Gaokao is next month. How's your review going?"

Tao Xue replied, "Sigh. My scores in the three mock exams were all above the first-tier university line. But just for an ordinary first-tier one, it'll be incredibly difficult to get into Sichuan University. Senior, I won't be able to go to Peking University with you."

"Haha, other first-tier universities are great too. Just focus on your review and the Gaokao, don't overthink it." The main purpose of Chen Guilong's text was to reassure her; the Gaokao was a once-in-a-lifetime event.

Tao Xue replied, "Got my food, looking for a seat now."

Chen Guilong put down his phone and started to eat.

Dong Qianqiu came over with his tray and sat down next to Chen Guilong. "I've finally finished revising my graduation thesis. The defense is in a few days."

"I'm jealous," Chen Guilong said with a smile. "I don't even know if I'll be able to graduate smoothly."

"You'll definitely graduate," Dong Qianqiu said.

Xu Fengyin, carrying her tray, passed by their table. She glanced at Chen Guilong and then went to sit at the next table.

Tao Xue had probably found a seat too, as she sent another text to complain, "You have no idea how hot it is this year, it hasn't rained for two months. The man-made lake at school has dried up to barely a foot deep. Ugh, and there's no air conditioning in the classrooms, I'm sweating all over every day during class."

"You can do it, just hang in there for a little over a week," Chen Guilong encouraged her.

Tao Xue said, "In the third mock exam's Chinese paper, the essay was about 'striving'. They gave two pieces of material, and one of them was actually about you. Haha."

Chen Guilong typed while chewing his food, "The mock exams are set by the city, so it's normal for them to use me as essay material."

"Senior, you're awesome!"

"Girls shouldn't use vulgar words."

"Hmph."

They texted back and forth for a good ten minutes before Tao Xue finally finished her meal and went back to the classroom for self-study.

Chen Guilong also returned to school and properly attended his classes in the evening.

In the blink of an eye, May passed.

This was quite normal.

Because the ones cooperating with Fenbei Wang were the local branches of China Mobile and China Unicom. The headquarters didn't want to blow the matter up and directly ordered the branches to behave.

17171's online game rankings for May were also released.

*World of Warcraft* was first, *Fantasy Westward Journey* second; the positions of the top two were unshakable.

*Crazyracing Kartrider* had actually surged to third.

*Audition Online* had fought its way to fourth.

*Legends of the Three Kingdoms* was in an unprecedented fifth place.

This was because Jay Chou's endorsement had been secured, and *Cao Cao* had also become the theme song for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*. The online licensed version of *Cao Cao* had an ad at the beginning of the song, which attracted many of Jay Chou's fans to start playing *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*.

Following that was *QQ Fantasy* in sixth, and *Quan Yu Tian Xia* in seventh.

*Zhengtu* was eighth. *The World of Legend* was ninth. *The Legend of Mir* was tenth.

*Yulgang* was completely crushed; you could barely find any active players in the game now.

There were still people bad-mouthing Shanda and crazily praising how awesome Chen Guilong was.

But Chen Guilong knew that either *The World of Legend* or *The Legend of Mir* alone could make enough profit to thrash *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*.

Moreover, *Quan Yu Tian Xia* was also in great danger; *Zhengtu*'s promotional offensive was just too fierce.

Tao Chenggang, however, had left the company to his subordinates and rushed back to his hometown to cheer for his younger sister's Gaokao.

(End of this chapter)
